participants.note: Concept ACKed, suggested considering clang-tidy tooling and noted extra getter candidates
Concept ACKed, raised concerns about proxy isolation, consensus GetOp return handling, and descriptor cache handling
Approved with comments; objected to Assume/Assert in consensus CountWitnessSigOps triggering library dependency issues

claims.harm: proxy.m_tor_stream_isolation was not conditional on is_valid
claims.settled_by_quote: Yeah, but I guess `std::optional` could make more sense. Done in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34741 and moved this into draft for now. edit: now merged

claims.harm: declaring nodiscard but casting to void in consensus code discards safety guarantees
claims.quote: I'm uncomfortable with both declaring `[[nodiscard] bool GetOp(...)` and then discarding the return value in consensus code (or non-test code in general).

claims.harm: descriptor cache misses or invalid cached pubkeys are not handled properly
using Assume or Assert introduces unwanted library dependencies into libbitcoin_consensus or inconsistent release/debug behavior
claims.quote: I don't think it makes sense to use Assume here. Logically `CountWitnessSigOps` could either be intended to tolerate malformed scripts, in which case it should ignore the GetOp return value, or intended not to tolerate them, in which case it should abort or raise an exception.

support.reason: This looks like a good thing to add, but I wonder if handling these cases incrementally is the correct approach.
FIrst commit does not seem right to me but otherwise these are nice changes that could prevent bugs.

result.notes: Initial assessment. Multiple concerns from ajtowns were addressed by pushing fixes or spinning off PR #34741. ryanofsky raised an objection regarding Assume/Assert in libbitcoin_consensus (CountWitnessSigOps), which caused check-deps failures in CI; the author agreed to use assert for now, but a fix has not yet been pushed, leaving the claim open.
